title: Pokémon Wildclash
description: Original Kanto Pokémon, cinematic live-action battles, classic commands and realistic elemental attacks.

genesis.worldPrompt: High overhead 35mm camera, downward 65 degrees, ground fills frame. Red: NEAR LOWER-LEFT x25%, y70%, rear three-quarter facing upper-right. Blue: FAR UPPER-RIGHT x76%, y32%, front three-quarter facing lower-left. Full bodies, at most two Pokémon. Kanto trainers behind, League caps, gloves, backpacks and Poké Ball belts. Hyperreal anatomy and woodland materials. Dramatic attacks, explosive acceleration, one crescendo, weighted recovery. Preserve outcomes. No UI or subtitles. Speak accepted English lines once. Merge compatible unsubmitted send-outs into one urgent shot with empty opening positions and overlapping releases. Attacks stay separate. Urgent video starts immediately with a ready clean BEFORE-action image, otherwise continue linked. Prepare fresh images ahead and during prior clips. The LLM calls cache_image; the server generates and saves it. After fainting, recall the entire Pokémon through a red beam into its ball, then close it. Keep the winner visible. Announce battle begins after send-out playback. Vary idle details. Group prose: overview/style; each team with trainer, position and opening state; camera/environment once; action.

animateBattles.description: Show accepted moves in the shared live video stream
animateBattles.label: Animate Battles

rejoinCooldownSeconds.label: Rejoin Cooldown
rejoinCooldownSeconds.description: Cooldown in seconds after fainting before rejoining

turnSeconds.label: Command Timer
turnSeconds.description: Seconds to choose a command. At zero, use the selected available move. Zero disables the timer.

battleCamera.label: Battle framing
battleCamera.description: Elevated downward view keeps both Pokémon inside the lower-left and upper-right quadrants.
battleCamera.default: High overhead 35mm battle camera pitched downward 65 degrees onto the clearing. Ground fills the frame; keep the horizon and sky above the crop. Red is the NEAR foreground Pokémon, LOWER-LEFT at x25%, y70%, rear three-quarter facing upper-right. Blue is the FAR background Pokémon, UPPER-RIGHT at x76%, y32%, front three-quarter facing lower-left. Blue stands several body lengths farther from the lens; perspective makes an equally sized creature smaller there. Show backs, heads and feet from above, with both full bodies inside their quadrants and open diagonal ground between them. Trainers stay behind their own Pokémon. Exactly one Pokémon per occupied side, at most two total. Preserve identities and scale through each shot. At a fresh-frame cut, establish this overhead composition immediately.

videoActionTiming.label: Video action timing
videoActionTiming.description: Action choreography across delayed continuous video chunks.
videoActionTiming.default: Attacks are dramatic, energetic and beautiful: explosive acceleration, powerful windup, one clear elemental crescendo and impactful contact around two seconds, then weighted recovery. Use brilliant fire and embers, branching electricity, translucent water, glittering spray, crystalline frost, volumetric light and wind-driven dust as appropriate to the accepted move. Preserve the recorded hit, miss, immunity, HP and winner. Effects remain light, water, debris or energy; keep one creature body per side. One accepted move per 5.17-second shot. Trainer callout and windup start in the first second, contact around two seconds, then the recorded reaction. A knockout is followed immediately by one protected urgent Poké Ball recall shot. First second: gentle breathing, the trainer kneels and aims the ball. Seconds one to four: a red beam shrinks the entire fainted Pokémon into flowing light and draws it completely into the ball. Final second: close and hold the ball. Keep the winner visible. Admit the next trainer after recall playback finishes. Idle shots show breathing, wind, foliage and settling dust. All speech is English. Wordless shots state: No words are spoken. Hold the high overhead view and near-left/far-right depth throughout.

visualContext.label: Generate setup frames
visualContext.description: Prepare a library of scene-only lineup and aftermath checkpoints ahead of events, then apply matching frames at safe stream boundaries.

setupImagePrompt.label: Scene start frame prompt
setupImagePrompt.default: High overhead 35mm battle camera pitched downward 65 degrees onto the clearing. Ground fills the frame; keep the horizon and sky above the crop. Red is the NEAR foreground Pokémon, LOWER-LEFT at x25%, y70%, rear three-quarter facing upper-right. Blue is the FAR background Pokémon, UPPER-RIGHT at x76%, y32%, front three-quarter facing lower-left. Blue stands several body lengths farther from the lens; perspective makes an equally sized creature smaller there. Show backs, heads and feet from above, with both full bodies inside their quadrants and open diagonal ground between them. Trainers stay behind their own Pokémon. Exactly one Pokémon per occupied side, at most two total. Preserve identities and scale through each shot. At a fresh-frame cut, establish this overhead composition immediately. Rebuild the reference from above. Hyperrealistic live-action fantasy cinematography. Recognizable first-generation Kanto Pokémon with believable biology, natural proportions, detailed scales, fur, wet skin, weathered shell and wing membranes. Rugged woodland clearing, wet earth, moss, distant mist, warm low sun and cool shadows. Real mass, inertia, contact shadows, physically grounded fire, turbulent water, branching electricity, airborne debris and environmental reactions. Photographic creature effects, cinematic contrast and restrained color. Show only the accepted lineup in settled poses. Match iconic species silhouettes with natural biological materials. Physical scene only, no UI, HUD, health bars, levels, numbers, text, labels, captions, menus, buttons, icons or watermark. Reconstruct clean scenery beneath reference graphics. Internal starting frame only. Trainers wear recognizable Kanto travel outfits: red-and-white League cap, red jacket, black shirt, blue jeans and yellow backpack on the near side; spiky auburn hair, cobalt-blue jacket, dark trousers and tan bag on the far side. Both wear fingerless gloves and Poké Ball belts.

imageGenerationPolicy.label: When to generate start frames
imageGenerationPolicy.default: Prepare fresh clean BEFORE-action images ahead of send-outs, attacks and items, and while the preceding urgent clip runs. Use an exact ready image for the accepted cast and physical posture. Urgent video generation starts immediately; if its image is unfinished or failed, continue linked from the preceding actual frame. Never wait for an image on the urgent path. Rebuild from the original clean arena reference to avoid accumulated errors. Compatible unsubmitted send-outs share a joint image with both releasing positions empty and each trainer holding a closed ball. Attack images contain no future impact or damage. Each resolved turn prepares a new checkpoint. Background preparation preserves the live feed. Recall stays linked after fainting and keeps the winner visible.

actionDrivenVideo.label: Prioritize battle actions
actionDrivenVideo.description: Legacy setting. Continuous idle animation remains enabled by the host.

damageMultiplier.label: Attack damage
damageMultiplier.description: Multiply calculated attack damage to give battles more rounds.

maxHitHpFraction.label: Maximum damage per hit
maxHitHpFraction.description: Cap one attack at this fraction of the target’s full HP, including critical and super-effective hits.
